summary.en: The most famous of the philhellenes. He came to Messolonghi in January 1824 with money and a plan to take Lepanto, and died of fever there in April. His death turned European opinion decisively toward the Greek cause.

body_html.en:
Byron had travelled in Greece in 1809 and 1810 and made it, through Childe Harold, the setting of Romantic longing for a whole generation of readers. When the London Greek Committee looked for a public face for its loan in 1823, he was the obvious choice.

He reached Messolonghi in January 1824, paid the Souliot troops from his own pocket, and tried to hold together a faction-ridden command. He fell ill in April and died on the 19th, before the loan money arrived. The effect on Greek fund-raising and on the diplomacy of the Powers was greater than anything he could have achieved alive.

title.en: The Death of Byron at Messolonghi
